examples.title: Crank-rocker four-bar
examples.description: A Grashof crank-rocker with a coupler point: the crank turns fully, the rocker swings. Coupler curve, transmission angle, Grashof label.

examples.title: Double-rocker four-bar
examples.description: A non-Grashof four-bar: no link can turn fully, the input rocks between two lock-up angles.

examples.title: Drag-link (double-crank)
examples.description: The shortest link is the frame: both cranks turn fully, the output speed varies during the turn.

examples.title: Change-point parallelogram linkage
examples.description: Equal opposite links: s + l = p + q. The coupler stays parallel to the frame (translates on circles).

examples.title: Slider-crank engine
examples.description: A single-cylinder engine: piston kinematics, a gas-pressure curve, indicated torque and flywheel energy fluctuation.

examples.title: Whitworth quick-return mechanism
examples.description: A crank drives a slotted lever that turns fully; the ram strokes slowly forward and returns quickly (ratio 2.26).

examples.title: Scotch yoke
examples.description: A pin in a slot drives a yoke in exact simple harmonic motion.

examples.title: Peaucellier-Lipkin inversor
examples.description: Seven bars turn a circle into an exact straight line (inversion about O).

examples.title: Watt's linkage
examples.description: Two rockers and a coupler: the coupler midpoint follows an approximate straight line.

examples.title: Pantograph
examples.description: A parallelogram scaled about a fixed pivot: the tracer draws a copy twice the size.

examples.title: Windscreen-wiper linkage
examples.description: A crank-rocker whose rocker is extended into a wiper arm with a blade.

examples.title: Theo Jansen's walking linkage
examples.description: One leg of the Strandbeest: eleven bars turn a crank into a walking foot path.

examples.title: Geneva drive
examples.description: A four-slot Geneva wheel indexing 90° per turn of the driver; analysed through the engaged window.

examples.title: Cam: 3-4-5 polynomial rise-dwell-return
examples.description: A translating roller follower rising 25 mm in 120°, dwelling 60°, returning in 120° with 3-4-5 polynomials.

examples.file: 15 Cam - cycloidal vs harmonic, roller follower.kmech
examples.title: Cam: cycloidal vs harmonic, roller follower
examples.description: The same rise-dwell-return with a cycloidal law (smooth) compared with simple harmonic motion (acceleration jump).

examples.title: Cam: flat-face follower, modified trapezoid
examples.description: A flat-faced translating follower (zero pressure angle) with a modified-trapezoid rise and return.

examples.title: Cam: swing-arm roller follower
examples.description: An oscillating roller follower (arm 70 mm) swinging 25° with harmonic motion.

examples.title: Spur gear pair 20/40, 20°
examples.description: The standard module-2 pair: d 40/80, contact ratio 1.6, centre distance 60 mm.

examples.title: Profile-shifted pinion (12/40)
examples.description: A 12-tooth pinion would be undercut; a profile shift of +0.4 on the pinion and −0.4 on the gear fixes it at the standard centre distance.

examples.title: Compound gear train 9:1
examples.description: Two stages (18→54 and 20→60) on a common intermediate shaft: speed and torque of every shaft.

examples.title: Gear train with an idler
examples.description: An idler reverses the sense of rotation without changing the ratio.

examples.file: 22 Planetary gearset - ratios with each member fixed.kmech
examples.title: Planetary gearset: ratios with each member fixed
examples.description: Sun 24, ring 72, three 24-tooth planets: the Willis equation for every fixed member.

examples.title: Helical gear pair
examples.description: Module 2, 15° helix: transverse module, contact ratios and virtual teeth.

examples.title: Belt and chain drives
examples.description: An open belt between 200 and 80 mm pulleys and a roller chain between 17 and 41 sprockets.
